claimBoundary: The two full-resolution chroma truths and the full-resolution luma are fixed before evaluation. Both chroma truths must collapse to the same low-resolution samples under the same integer 2:1 box average.

The phase-shifted thin stripe must have lower source-truth RMSE under centered 3/4-1/4 reconstruction than under nearest/current reconstruction. The true low-resolution plateau must prefer the opposite reconstruction, with nearest/current exact.

Because a deterministic decoder limited to the shared subsampled chroma observes identical chroma inputs in the two worlds, it cannot select the source-truth-optimal reconstruction for both. Keeping full-resolution luma identical strengthens the counterexample: luma guidance only resolves the ambiguity under an additional luma/chroma correlation prior.

This is an identifiability mechanism result, not a claim that centered or nearest interpolation is perceptually optimal on natural images. Any production adaptive policy must state its prior/objective and carry counterexamples where that prior fails.
